name: Orange Blossom Honey
description: The quintessential varietal honey for traditional meads. Produced from the nectar of citrus groves, offering bright citrus zest notes, white floral perfume, and clean sweetness. World-renowned in BJCP competition judging.
fermentationBehavior: Retains delicate citrus blossom aromas best when fermented cool (60–65°F). Avoid boiling to prevent driving off volatile citrus terpenes. Moderate nutrient requirement.
pairingNotes: Outstanding on its own in Traditional Mead. Superb with stone fruits (peaches, apricots), citrus zest, ginger, and oak aging.

name: Sweet Clover Honey
description: Classic North American honey variety noted for its subtle vanilla and sweet spice cinnamon undertones caused by natural coumarin compounds in sweet clover blossoms. Produces pale, soft, delicate meads.
fermentationBehavior: Ferments cleanly with neutral yeast strains. High glucose content causes fast crystallization in raw state, but dissolves rapidly in must. Very low residual harshness.
pairingNotes: Excellent delicate base for berry melomels (blackberry, raspberry), light metheglins, and dry sparkling meads.

name: White Dutch Clover Honey
description: The benchmark everyday table honey and common mead base. Extremely pale with a pristine, mild floral sweetness and faint pasture grass notes. Allows fruit and spices in melomels to take center stage.
fermentationBehavior: Clean, predictable fermentation with moderate nitrogen demand. Very pale straw color persists in finished dry mead.
pairingNotes: Ideal neutral canvas for fruit meads (cherries, berries, currants) and cysers. Does not clash with adjuncts.

name: Tupelo Honey
origin: Apalachicola River Basin, Florida, United States
description: Celebrated 'Queen of Honeys', harvested from White Ogeechee Tupelo trees in remote Gulf Coast river swamps. Renowned for its rich floral bouquet, soft pear/melon fruitiness, and unique resistance to crystallization.
fermentationBehavior: Remarkably stable must with high fructose ratio. Retains round mouthfeel and pleasant body even when fermented to bone-dry final gravity.
pairingNotes: Exceptional in Semi-Sweet Traditional Mead (M1B). Complements stone fruits, vanilla bean, and light French oak aging.

name: Meadowfoam Honey
description: Cult-favorite artisanal honey harvested from white meadowfoam fields in Oregon. Delivers an astonishingly distinct toasted marshmallow, crème brûlée, and vanilla sugar flavor profile that is utterly unique in meadmaking.
fermentationBehavior: Toasted marshmallow and vanilla notes persist with great fidelity through primary fermentation. Ferment with clean ale or wine yeast; keep nutrient additions balanced.
pairingNotes: Magnificent in Sweet Traditional Mead (M1C) and dessert meads. Pairs gorgeously with cacao nibs, toasted coconut, cold brew coffee, and bourbon barrels.

name: Buckwheat Honey (Eastern)
description: Deep blackish-amber honey packed with iron, minerals, and polyphenols. Noted for its intense, pungent aroma reminiscent of wet horse blanket, barnyard, molasses, and malted grain. Highly prized for robust specialty meads and braggots.
fermentationBehavior: Mellows significantly with 12–24 months of aging as pungent volatile sulfur/phenolic compounds oxidize and integrate into dark cherry and leather tones. Extremely high mineral content buffers fermentation pH.
pairingNotes: Ideal for Braggot (M4A) grist pairings (roasted barley, chocolate malt), dark winter metheglins, cherries, and smoked malts.

name: Buckwheat Honey (Western / Coast)
description: Harvested from wild California buckwheat chaparral rather than cultivated grain. Slightly lighter than Eastern buckwheat with pronounced dried fruit, pipe tobacco, toffee, and herbal nuances rather than heavy barnyard notes.
fermentationBehavior: Ferments vigorously; develops rich dark toffee and dried fig complex character with moderate conditioning time.
pairingNotes: Superb for dark bochet styles, fig/plum melomels, and bourbon barrel-aged sack meads.

name: Northeastern Wildflower Honey
botanicalSource: Aster, Goldenrod, Dandelion, Basswood & Berry Flora
description: Complex autumn wildflower blend from mixed forest edges and meadows. Displays amber depth, layered dried fruit, autumnal honey character, and subtle goldenrod spice.
fermentationBehavior: Consistent and reliable fermentation. Blended polyfloral nectar buffers must and provides balanced natural trace nutrients.
pairingNotes: Versatile all-around mead honey. Pairs exceptionally well with apples in Cyser (M2A/C2B), mixed berries, and holiday spice blends.

name: Pacific Northwest Wildflower Honey
description: Bright, aromatic wildflower honey collected from mountain foothills and coastal valleys. Imparts notes of fresh bramble berries, evergreen woods, and crisp floral nectar.
fermentationBehavior: Retains delicate red fruit notes and bright natural acidity during fermentation.
pairingNotes: Natural synergy with marionberries, blackberries, raspberries, and tart cherries in Berry Meads (M2C).

name: Ling Heather Honey
description: Legendary European moorland honey, famous for its thixotropic (jelly-like) consistency that liquifies when stirred. Deep amber with pungent floral, peat smoke, malted heather, and woody herbal complexity.
fermentationBehavior: Requires vigorous stirring or warming to dissolve into must. Contains high natural protein and minerals that build exceptional mouthfeel and silky body in mead.
pairingNotes: Historic choice for Scottish Heather Mead, strong metheglins with gorse/myrtle, and dark traditional sack meads. Pairs wonderfully with peat-smoked whiskey casks.

name: Acacia (Black Locust) Honey
description: Among the palest and most delicate honeys in the world. Water-white with a crystalline appearance, mild vanilla blossom aroma, and exceptionally high fructose content that keeps it liquid for years.
fermentationBehavior: Extremely clean fermentation without phenolic harshness. Because of its ultra-delicate character, use subtle wine yeast (e.g. Lalvin ICV D47 or DV10) and low fermentation temperatures.
pairingNotes: Benchmark choice for crisp, delicate Dry Traditional Meads (M1A). Also complements fragile botanicals like elderflower or chamomile.

name: Linden / Basswood Honey
origin: Great Lakes Basin, United States & Eastern Europe
description: Harvested from blooming linden (lime tree) blossoms in early summer. Prized for its unmistakable fresh mint, wintergreen, lime blossom, and herbal cooling sensation that carries through fermentation.
fermentationBehavior: The crisp menthol/cooling herbal signature is persistent and refreshing in finished mead. Ferments cleanly and brightens traditional mead acidity.
pairingNotes: Superb for refreshing summer hydromels, citrus metheglins, green tea meads, and crisp semi-sweet traditionals.

name: Black Button Sage Honey
origin: Central & Southern California Coast, United States
description: Premium California coastal honey with very high fructose levels that prevent granulation. Despite coming from a sage plant, it has a wonderfully smooth, sweet, non-herbal floral flavor with a velvety finish.
fermentationBehavior: Ferments with exceptional clarity and round body. The high F/G ratio imparts a smooth perceived residual sweetness even at low gravity.
pairingNotes: Outstanding in Traditional Meads (M1A/M1B). Blends well with lavender, citrus, and light berry adjuncts.

name: Sourwood Honey
origin: Appalachian Mountains, North Carolina & Georgia, United States
description: High-altitude mountain honey harvested from sourwood trees blooming along Appalachian ridges. Celebrated for its unique gingerbread, cinnamon, maple, and slight tart apple finish.
fermentationBehavior: Produces meads of stunning balance. The natural tart acidity offsets sweetness, giving finished mead crisp definition and longevity.
pairingNotes: Exceptional in Semi-Sweet and Sweet Traditional Meads, autumn spiced metheglins, and charred oak barrel aging.

name: Avocado Blossom Honey
origin: Southern California, United States & Michoacán, Mexico
description: Inky dark honey produced from avocado orchards. Possesses a rich, molasses-like profile with notes of dried plum, caramel, dark malt syrup, and hints of savory umami.
fermentationBehavior: Does not taste like avocado fruit. Ferments into rich, full-bodied dark meads with stout-like depth and smooth maltiness.
pairingNotes: Excellent for Braggot (M4A), bochet styles, dark winter metheglins with vanilla, and aging on toasted oak cubes.

name: Mesquite Honey
origin: Sonoran & Chihuahuan Deserts, United States & Mexico
description: Harvested from desert mesquite blooms in the American Southwest. Pale with a delicate floral aroma and distinct pleasant undertones of raw agave, toasted grains, and faint desert smoke.
fermentationBehavior: Low moisture desert honey with high sugar density. Dissolves cleanly and produces bright, warm, aromatic meads.
pairingNotes: Pairs beautifully with prickly pear cactus in Melomel, chipotle/ancho peppers in Capsicumel (M3A), and reposado tequila barrel aging.

name: Macadamia Blossom Honey
description: Rich amber tropical honey collected from blooming macadamia nut groves. Features unmistakable nutty nuances, toasted praline, dark sugar, and a round buttery finish.
fermentationBehavior: Adds considerable perceived body and nut complexity to fermented mead without adding oil or head-retention killing fatty acids.
pairingNotes: Fabulous in dessert meads, toasted nut metheglins, passionfruit/guava melomels, and bourbon barrel-aged sack meads.

name: Fireweed Honey
origin: Alaska & Pacific Northwest, United States & British Columbia, Canada
description: Known as the 'Champagne of Honeys', produced from magenta fireweed blossoms colonizing boreal forest burns. Water-white to very pale, offering delicate peach, green tea, and floral notes.
fermentationBehavior: Very clean, gentle fermentation. Retains high clarity and light straw brightness, ideal for sparkling champagne-style mead.
pairingNotes: Best in Dry Sparkling Traditional Mead (M1A). Complements delicate alpine herbs, white peaches, and pear cysers.

name: Lavender Honey
description: Prized Mediterranean honey harvested from lavender fields in southern France. Imparts a distinctive aromatic perfume of fresh lavender blossoms, sweet wood, and faint lemon herbal tea without soapiness.
fermentationBehavior: The floral lavender aromatics are surprisingly stable through cool fermentation, providing natural floral lift without needing post-fermentation dry herb steeping.
pairingNotes: Fabulous in traditional semi-sweet mead, lemon metheglin, blueberry melomel, and goat cheese companion pairings.

name: Sweet Chestnut Honey
description: Distinctive European dark honey renowned for its assertive herbal bitterness, high natural tannins, roasted chestnut, and dark wood character. Stays liquid indefinitely thanks to high fructose levels.
fermentationBehavior: Adds notable tannic structure, bitterness, and dark amber color to finished mead. The natural astringency balances sweet high-gravity sack meads.
pairingNotes: Superb for high-gravity Sack Meads (M1C), Braggots (M4A), and pairings with roasted autumn spices and bitter orange peel.

name: Eucalyptus Honey (Blue Gum)
origin: Tasmania & Victoria, Australia & California, United States
description: Amber honey from Tasmanian blue gum and coastal eucalyptus blossoms. Delivers a bold, aromatic profile featuring eucalyptol, menthol, butterscotch, and warm damp cedarwood.
fermentationBehavior: Eucalyptol and terpene compounds persist strongly; use carefully or blend with neutral clover honey to avoid medicinal harshness.
pairingNotes: Works wonderfully in spiced metheglins with ginger, lemon, and honey-menthol soothing winter beverages, or bold hopped meads.

name: Manuka Honey
description: World-famous New Zealand honey harvested from native manuka tea trees. Celebrated for its unique antibacterial methylglyoxal (MGO) content, thixotropic body, earthy damp humus, and resinous herbal taste.
fermentationBehavior: Heavy thixotropic body requires thorough mixing with warm water. Produces an intense, earthy, savory mead with pronounced resinous phenolic notes.
pairingNotes: Best for complex experimental specialty meads, spiced herbal metheglins, and braggots. Often blended with clover to temper intensity.

name: Blackberry Blossom Honey
description: Harvested from wild Himalayan blackberry briars flowering across western Oregon and Washington. Light amber with rich fruitiness, red berry essence, and soft floral finish.
fermentationBehavior: Clean fermentation with moderate acidity that enhances the perception of fresh berry fruitiness in the finished beverage.
pairingNotes: The premier honey choice for Blackberry Melomel (M2C), fruit meads, and summer berry cysers.

name: Raspberry Blossom Honey
origin: Pacific Northwest, United States & Quebec, Canada
description: Collected from cultivated and wild red raspberry cane fields. Very pale amber with a mellow, round mouthfeel and subtle raspberry and rose petal floral undertones.
fermentationBehavior: Ferments with high clarity and pleasant soft fruit aromatics that linger in the head space.
pairingNotes: Magnificent in Raspberry Melomel (Framboise mead, M2C), hibiscus metheglin, and white wine yeast fermentations.

name: Alfalfa Honey
description: Extremely popular light Western honey produced from blooming alfalfa hay fields. Clean, mild, delicately sweet with subtle hints of fresh beeswax and green meadow grasses.
fermentationBehavior: Rapidly granulating honey in raw form due to low F/G ratio; readily liquefies in water. Very clean fermentation profile.
pairingNotes: Versatile neutral base for melomels, fruit wines, and light summer session hydromels.

name: Cotton Blossom Honey
origin: Texas, Mississippi Delta & San Joaquin Valley, United States
description: Harvested from cotton blossoms and extrafloral nectaries of cotton plants. Very pale with a soft, confectionary marshmallow and powdered sugar profile.
fermentationBehavior: Ferments cleanly with gentle residual confectionary character.
pairingNotes: Great affordable substitute for meadowfoam when looking for confectionary marshmallow notes in sweet and dessert meads.

name: Dandelion Honey
description: Vibrant golden-amber honey harvested from early spring dandelion blooms. Assertive and sharp with a distinctive aroma of fresh dandelion greens, ammonia, yellow pollen, and tart herbal honey.
fermentationBehavior: Granulates almost instantly after extraction. Sharp sulfur/ammonia aroma in raw honey completely blows off during fermentation, leaving bright herbal citrus flavors.
pairingNotes: Fabulous in citrus metheglins, herbal spring meads, and farmhouse braggots.

name: Yellow Star Thistle Honey
origin: Northern California & Pacific Northwest, United States
description: Prized prize-winning varietal honey harvested in late summer from yellow star thistle blooms. Extra white to light amber with clean floral sweetness and distinctive hints of anise, cinnamon, and almond.
fermentationBehavior: One of the most reliable and beloved honeys in American home meadmaking. Ferments with brilliant clarity and delicate spice aromatics.
pairingNotes: Superb in Dry and Semi-Sweet Traditional Meads (M1A/M1B) and spiced metheglins with cinnamon and clove.

name: Wild Thyme Honey
description: Ancient and revered Greek honey collected from wild mountain thyme blooming under intense Mediterranean sun. Deep golden amber with explosive resinous herbal aromas, thyme essential oil, and spicy balsamic depth.
fermentationBehavior: Extremely high concentration of natural thymol and volatile essential oils that remain prominent throughout fermentation.
pairingNotes: Historic base for Mediterranean Metheglin (M3A), lemon meads, pomegranate melomels, and pairing with salty cheeses.

name: Pine / Fir Honeydew Honey
botanicalSource: Marchalina hellenica secretions on Pinus halepensis
description: Known as Waldhonig (Forest Honey). Sourced not from blossom nectar, but from honeydew secretions collected by bees on conifers. Rich, dark reddish-brown with aromas of pine needle, forest floor, malt, and caramelized wood.
fermentationBehavior: Extremely high in minerals and oligosaccharides with lower simple sugar percentage. Builds immense mouthfeel and malty depth.
pairingNotes: Outstanding for Braggot (M4A), smoked specialty meads, and winter dark meads paired with spices and dark malts.

name: Beechwood Honeydew Honey
botanicalSource: Ultracoelostoma assimile secretions on Nothofagus solandri
description: Collected from ancient black beech forests in New Zealand. Lustrous dark amber honey rich in complex prebiotic oligosaccharides, with deep flavors of treacle, toasted barley, and wet river stones.
fermentationBehavior: Slow to granulate. Low sweetness perception due to complex sugars; finishes clean and malty in meads and braggots.
pairingNotes: Ideal for Scottish and English style Braggots, barrel-aged bochet meads, and dark holiday melomels with figs and plums.

name: Oak Honeydew Honey
botanicalSource: Lachnus roboris secretions on Quercus robur / Quercus ilex
description: Dark, almost black honeydew honey produced in European oak forests. Rich in natural polyphenols, dry oak tannins, molasses, and roasted chicory with very little cloying sweetness.
fermentationBehavior: Produces structured, dry, wine-like meads with natural wood tannins that emulate extended barrel aging.
pairingNotes: Exceptional in bold Sack Meads, Braggots, blackberry melomels, and dark metheglins with clove and star anise.

name: Cranberry Blossom Honey
description: Rare honey harvested from commercial cranberry bogs during early summer pollination. Reddish-amber with crisp tartness, red currant fruit, and a pleasant dry cranberry finish.
fermentationBehavior: High natural malic/citric acidity complements fermentation, yielding zesty, refreshing meads with great palate cleansing ability.
pairingNotes: Natural match for Cyser (M2A / C2B), tart berry melomels, and holiday cranberry-orange spiced metheglins.

name: Saw Palmetto Honey
description: Harvested from wild saw palmetto palms across the Florida peninsula. Rich amber color with warm butterscotch, caramelized cane sugar, baked fruit, and pleasant woody undertones.
fermentationBehavior: Ferments into full-bodied, warm amber mead with lingering toffee richness.
pairingNotes: Great for Semi-Sweet and Sweet Traditional Meads, stone fruit melomels, and dark spiced metheglins.

name: Apple Blossom Honey
origin: Hudson Valley, New York & Normandy, France
description: Delicate, precious honey harvested from commercial apple orchards during brief spring bloom. White to extra light amber with crisp aromas of fresh green apple, orchard blossoms, and mild citrus.
fermentationBehavior: Light, clean fermentation with delicate ester profile. High natural malic acid enhances crispness in finished beverage.
pairingNotes: The definitive, ultimate honey for Cyser (M2A / C2B). Blends seamlessly with freshly pressed apple cider and french oak.

name: Goldenrod Honey
origin: Midwest & Northeastern United States & Eastern Canada
description: Harvested from brilliant yellow goldenrod blooming in late autumn fields. Amber in color with a notoriously pungent, spicy, musky raw aroma that ages into magnificent warm butterscotch, peppery spice, and herbal character in finished mead.
fermentationBehavior: Raw honey often has a strong barnyard musky scent that disappears during fermentation and cellar aging, transforming into rich autumnal spice.
pairingNotes: Exceptional in Autumn Spiced Metheglins (M3A), dark winter cysers, and robust braggots.
